defect: The new HTTP metadata cache (file_handle_cache in the shared HTTPFileSystem) is read and written from HTTPFileHandle::Initialize without any lock and its entries never expire, so concurrent opens race on the unordered_map and stale length/last_modified values are served.
reason: The fix adds file_handle_cache_lock around the lookup and the insert and a max-age check, repairing the unsynchronized, never-invalidated cache that this change added (the intermediate commit had only commented out the lookup, the racy write stayed).

defect: For TINYINT/SMALLINT groups without statistics the change builds NumericStatistics with min = MinimumValue and max = MinimumValue (instead of MaximumValue), so the computed range collapses to a few bits and the perfect hash table is far too small for the actual values; required_bits is also left uninitialized when min/max are NULL.
reason: The fix replaces the second MinimumValue with MaximumValue and returns false for NULL min/max, both in lines this change added.

defect: ConvertVariantToValue indexes the VARIANT blob data with value_data[row] instead of value_data[value.sel->get_index(row)], reading the wrong blob (or out of bounds) for dictionary or constant input vectors.
reason: The line was first written by this change (every other access in the same function goes through sel->get_index) and the fix adds the missing selection-vector lookup.

defect: With the new debug_force_no_cross_product setting the optimizer throws InternalException("HyperGraph isn't connected") for any query whose relations are genuinely disconnected, e.g. SELECT 1 FROM (SELECT 1), (SELECT 1).
reason: The throw was added by this change and the fuzzer-driven fix replaces it with returning the unreordered plan, so a valid query no longer hits an internal error.

defect: In the no-NULL branch of RadixScatterListVector the DESC inversion now starts at key_location_start + 1 ('skip over validity byte'), but that branch has no validity byte, so the empty/non-empty list marker is no longer inverted and DESC ordering of empty versus non-empty lists is wrong.
reason: Before the change the no-NULL branch inverted all width bytes from offset 0; the change introduced the +1 and the fix restores the start at key_location_start.

defect: The rewritten Value::MAP(child_type, values) pushes children[0] into map_values as well as map_keys, so every map value is replaced by its key.
reason: The typo is in a line this change added and the fix changes it to children[1].

defect: MergeValidityRange stops only when tuples[i] > start + count, so an update at offset start + count (one past the requested range) is still merged and writes the validity bit one row beyond the range.
reason: The new range-merge function was added by this change with the off-by-one bound, and the fix changes > to >=.

defect: The new TPC-E test writes REQUIRE(1==0) without a trailing semicolon; Catch's REQUIRE expands to a do { } while (...) statement, so the file fails to compile (and the assertion would always fail).
reason: The broken statement is in the file this change created, and the fix (Fixes for GCC) adds the semicolon so the unittest binary builds with GCC.

defect: When an OR child compares a column with a NULL constant the change pushes IsNullFilter for IS DISTINCT FROM NULL and IsNotNullFilter for IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NULL (and also maps = NULL / <> NULL), which is the inverse of the SQL semantics and lets the zone-map filter prune row groups that contain matching rows.
reason: The mapping was introduced here, and after an intermediate commit dropped the EQUAL/NOTEQUAL cases the fix swaps IsNull and IsNotNull for the DISTINCT FROM cases.

defect: For constant input the change returns result.Reference(dict_child) turned into a CONSTANT_VECTOR, so the result shares the bind data's list-entry and validity buffers in which row 1 is marked NULL; Vector::Flatten of a non-null constant keeps that validity, so row 1 becomes NULL, and writes to the result would corrupt the shared bind data.
reason: The fix, which says it repairs a bug for constant input, replaces this with ConstantVector::Reference, which writes the list entry into the result's own buffer; the shared-vector construction was introduced by this change.

defect: The new ExecuteTernaryInternal and ExecuteQuaternaryInternal mark the result as constant and compute only one row when just a and b are constant, ignoring whether c (and d) are constant, so rows 1..count-1 are left unset when c or d vary.
reason: Both functions were added by this change with the copied binary constant check, and the fix extends the check to c and d.

defect: The change calls ExpressionIterator::EnumerateChildren without including duckdb/planner/expression_iterator.hpp (nothing it includes pulls that header in), so the file does not compile on its own in a non-unity build; it also includes a DuckDB header with angle brackets.
reason: The fix (fix headers) adds the missing expression_iterator.hpp include and switches bound_reference_expression.hpp to a quoted include, repairing the header problem this change introduced.

defect: TransformCatalogReservedSchemaTable builds TableDescription(catalog, catalog, table_name), passing the catalog as the schema and dropping the parsed schema for catalog.schema.table references.
reason: The typo is in a function this change added and the fix replaces the second catalog with schema.

defect: TryDequeueWithoutConcurrentPurge loads purge_active into the expected value and CASes it to true, so it also succeeds when a purge is already active, then dequeues concurrently with the purge and resets purge_active to false while the purge is still running.
reason: The broken atomic guard was added by this change, and the fix CASes from an expected value of false so the function waits until no purge is active.

defect: The new even() rounds incorrectly: for FLOAT/DOUBLE the check ceil(x) / 2 * 2 == ceil(x) is always true in floating point, so odd values are returned unchanged, and negative inputs are not rounded away from zero in the integral and decimal variants.
reason: All the operators were introduced by this change, and the fix replaces them with an int64-based operator that rounds odd values away from zero.
